acceptance_criteria: All approval, source, prior-reference, E1 environment, sensor, geometry and frozen-tool identities match before execution.
Exactly one existing source world and 24 fixed poses in an 8/8/8 role split are processed; no world or pose is regenerated or selected by scan quality.
The analytic six-ray box control has maximum distance error no greater than 1e-5 m.
Every scan is float32 range_m plus uint8 valid_mask with shape 16x720; every valid range is finite in [0.3,50] m and every invalid range is exactly 50 m.
Two fresh RaycastingScene instances have identical valid masks and maximum valid-range difference no greater than 1e-6 m for every pose.
Every valid mask equals its frozen prior reference and maximum valid-range difference is no greater than 1e-5 m.
All poses have at least 0.8 m horizontal clearance and all 5 m teacher branch rays are clear to target minus 0.25 m.
Exactly 24 diagnostic NPZ files, all-sample metrics, full-world pose map, 24-scan fixed-scale contact sheet, provenance, summary, immutable run state and evidence manifest exist.
Formal dataset, training, model, Isaac, Gazebo, topology and M-TARE counts all remain zero; total sealed run size does not exceed 0.05 GB.
baseline: Read-only 24-scan CPU reference from the prior failed Isaac smoke: valid ratio 0.990972--1.0, mean 0.997070, minimum horizontal clearance 2.058 m and 24/24 branch-line-of-sight checks passed. It remains diagnostic and cannot be promoted to training data.

environment.backend: CPU only, one process, numerical thread counts forced to 1

estimated_cost.compute: One CPU process in the frozen E1 environment; approximately 552,960 primary world rays across two fresh scenes plus clearance/branch audit rays and six analytic rays; no GPU, Docker, Isaac, Gazebo or training.

expected_evidence: Approved card/proposal, frozen run spec/command, source/tool/reference/environment hashes, raw log, duration, exit code, RUN_STATE and evidence manifest
Analytic control, exact pose manifest, 24 diagnostic scans and per-pose shape/range/hash/determinism/reference/clearance/branch metrics
One complete world pose map and one fixed-scale contact sheet containing all 24 scans, each with machine-readable provenance and limitations
Explicit zero formal-dataset/training/model/Isaac/Gazebo/topology/M-TARE counts and next-step authorization boundary
method: Use the exact existing Cano seed-0 native mesh, graph, splines, FTA and deterministic 24-pose 8/8/8 role manifest. First pass an analytic known-distance box control; then build two fresh Open3D 0.19.0 RaycastingScene instances and cast the exact 16x720 first-return grid at every pose with explicit 0.3--50 m validity. Compare independent scenes and all 24 prior frozen CPU references, verify 0.8 m horizontal clearance and 5 m oracle-branch line of sight, and preserve every diagnostic NPZ plus complete fixed-scale visual evidence. Generate no new world or formal dataset and train nothing.
question: Can the existing audited Cano seed-0 perception mesh produce deterministic, finite and topology-consistent 16x720 idealized LiDAR observations with Open3D CPU raycasting, without Isaac?
stop_conditions: Any approval, source, reference, environment, tool, command, scope or output-directory mismatch
Analytic control failure, pose/role/ray drift, shape/dtype/range violation, independent-scene mismatch or prior-reference drift
Any clearance or branch line-of-sight failure, missing complete visualization/provenance/evidence, timeout or disk-limit breach
Continuation would require a retry, new world, mesh repair, pose or threshold change, noise/randomization, Isaac, Gazebo, data export, training, topology or M-TARE work

user_authorization.confirmation_reference: 用户在收到完整输入、方法、样本数、成本、验收与停止边界后明确回复：继续做啊为啥这么容易停
user_authorization.scope: Exactly one execution of the frozen seed-0 Cano CPU raycast diagnostic contract: 1 existing world, 24 fixed poses, two independent 16x720 raycast passes, analytic control, prior-reference regression and complete visual evidence; zero formal dataset, training, model, Isaac, Gazebo, topology or M-TARE work.
